hints: Notice where the solid and dashed maximum curves cross the central line - X, R and two other points never move and are nodes.
Recall that in a stationary wave all points between two adjacent nodes move together, but points in the next loop move oppositely.
Compare the loop containing S above P with the loop containing T below Q and think which way each must move back toward zero after maximum displacement.
walkthrough: Identify nodes and antinodes from the diagram. The solid and dashed extremes intersect at X, at R and at two other points on XY, so these are nodes with zero amplitude.
Locate S and T. S is the peak of the leftmost loop at $t_0$ and T is the trough of the next loop at $t_0$, with node R between them.
State the stationary-wave rule: points within the same loop between two nodes are in phase, while points in adjacent loops separated by a node are in antiphase.
Apply the rule just after $t_0$. Both S and T must leave maximum displacement toward the mean position, so S moves down while T moves up - opposite directions.
This is option B. Node R stays undisplaced, PQ is $\lambda/2$, and symmetric points about R are in opposite loops and therefore out of phase.

options.A: Point R is on the central mean line where solid and dashed curves cross, so it is a node and remains at zero displacement.
options.B: S and T are antinodes in adjacent loops separated by node R, so they vibrate in antiphase and move toward the mean position in opposite directions after $t_0$.
options.C: P and Q are centres of adjacent antinodes, so distance PQ is half a loop spacing, equal to $\lambda/2$, not $\lambda$.
options.D: Equal distances on opposite sides of node R place the two points in adjacent loops, so they vibrate in antiphase, not in phase.
